thread:
Elaine (Sales): quick heads-up — Zenith signed a commit, asking for recommended reserved GPU footprint + autoscale rules for a 90-day POC. baseline ~1,000,000 tokens/day, expected 3x burst windows for marketing events. they want HA across us-east + europe-west. also asked for a cost estimate and an explanation of preheat behavior.
Tomas (SolutionsEng): got it. are those tokens uniformly distributed or spiky? any per-request length/seq expectations?
Elaine (Sales): mix — 70% short chat (avg 40 tokens), 30% long generation (avg 600 tokens). bursts up to ~3x mean qps for 2-4 hour windows. they want <250ms p50 for short chat.
Tomas (SolutionsEng): rough calc then. short chat qps ~ (0.7 * 1e6 tokens/day) / (40 tokens) / 86400s ≈ 201 qps baseline; long gen ~ (0.3 * 1e6) / 600 / 86400s ≈ 5.8 qps baseline. burst factor 3 => ~620 qps equivalent for short paths.
Maya (Infra): ok that's helpful. our recommended pattern for enterprise POC: reserve a modest pool sized for baseline + preheat capacity and rely on autoscale for bursts, with burst credits enabled. suggested starting point: reserve capacity for 1.5x baseline (to keep committed cost reasonable) and allow autoscale to 4x using burst credits during events.
Elaine (Sales): can you translate that to GPUs? customer is asking whether to reserve 4 or 8 A100s.
Tomas (SolutionsEng): depends on model variant. assume quantized MPT-like model throughput ~80 tok/s per GPU for long sequences when batching is effective; for short chat path (low-latency) we assume ~350 tok/s per GPU with small-batch fast path. Quick calc in case:
```
# baseline token load: 1,000,000 tokens/day ~ 11.57 tok/s on average
# but converting to qps for short chat: ~201 qps (see above)
# with 350 tok/s per GPU for low-latency, equivalent GPUs = short_path_tokps / 350
# using burst sizing: peak short qps ~620 -> 620 / (350/avg_tokens_per_req) (approx)
```
Tomas (SolutionsEng): concretely, for the mixed profile I'd propose reserving 4 GPUs: that covers ~1.5x baseline with room for KV-cache warmup and preheat across regions. Then a policy to autoscale up to 12 GPUs during events (burst credits + spot-backed dedicated if ok). 4 -> 12 gives ~3x headroom for the heavy windows.
Ben (Product): note that autoscale latency to ramp depends on prewarmed containers and KV cache state. if we rely on cold spin-up during a 2-hour spike they'll hit higher latency. preheat helps a lot.
Devon (CustomerSuccess): customer asked what "preheat" means operationally. can we give a one-paragraph explanation in the quote?
Maya (Infra): short answer for quote: "Preheat = proactively creating serving capacity and warming model KV caches/prefixes ahead of expected traffic. This reduces tail latency and avoids cold-start token penalties. We can preheat per-AZ or cross-region; preheat windows should be scheduled 15–30 minutes before expected peak for best results."
Sarah (Security): also confirm network constraints for cross-region: for Private deployment they need VPC peering and KMS key replication plan. Zenith flagged encryption-at-rest + key separation during POC.
Elaine (Sales): they will run POC in our Hosted Dedicated with VPC peering to their corp network. they want KMS integration and audit logs for all infer requests (token-level logging disabled).
Sarah (Security): audit logs for request metadata are fine; we should avoid storing user content. add the KMS integration checklist to the quote.
Tomas (SolutionsEng): back to numbers — if we reserve 4 GPUs and autoscale to 12, here's a quick cost delta sketch for 90 days: reserved 4 GPUs @ committed discount vs burst on-demand/spot for the extra 8. I can put actual $ once finance gives current reserved vs on-demand rates.
Elaine (Sales): please do — they want a line-item: reserved GPUs cost, burst/spot cushion, preheat windows (hours/day), and support SLA (canary deploys + fallback to smaller model).
Maya (Infra): operational checklist to include in POC runbook: 1) model pin/version, 2) KV-cache warmup script + sample prompt set, 3) autoscale policy (scale step: +2 GPUs / min; cooldown 10m), 4) burst credit pool (hours), 5) cross-region fallback (route to other region when AZ degraded).
Tomas (SolutionsEng): sample autoscale snippet for quote body:
```json
{
  "policy": "cpu-and-latency",
  "scale_step": 2,
  "max_instances": 12,
  "min_instances": 4,
  "cooldown_seconds": 600
}
```
Tomas (SolutionsEng): we should call out fallback model option (smaller quantized model) if autoscale cannot get capacity in <3 minutes.
Devon (CustomerSuccess): customer also asked about SLA during POC windows (uptime and p50/p95). what should we promise?
Ben (Product): for POC we can promise best-effort p50 targets and committed p95 only on dedicated reserved portion. recommend: p50 <250ms for short chat, p95 best-effort during burst unless they take higher reserved headroom. call out trade-offs in proposal.
Sarah (Security): add a note re: data handling — no user content persisted, telemetry only, KMS access logs provided. include contact for compliance questionnaire follow-up.
Elaine (Sales): perfect. Tomas/Maya can you draft the GPU/reservation + autoscale numbers + preheat hours and a short paragraph for the quote by EOD? I'll package with security checklist and pricing stub.
Tomas (SolutionsEng): on it, will post a draft config + cost placeholder here when ready.
Maya (Infra): working on the runbook bullets and KV warmup snippet.
deploy-bot: deployment scheduled for model-warmup-job to us-east and europe-west at 2024-10-02T14:30Z (preheat dry-run).
Elaine (Sales): :thumbsup: thanks team — I'll sync with Zenith PM tomorrow morning and feed back any extra asks.
